newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES WIN FIFTH STRAIGHT GAME.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES WIN FIFTH STRAIGHT GAME.

text.p: Tom Glavine allowed four hits over seven scoreless innings and Jeff Blauser went 4-for-4 with three runs as the Atlanta Braves won their fifth straight game, 4-2 over the Houston Astros on Tuesday.

Glavine (2-0) walked two and struck out four in improving to 8-10 lifetime against the Astros. He is the winningest pitcher in the major leagues since 1991, with 108 victories. Mark Wohlers struck out two in a perfect ninth inning for his third save.
Blauser has hit in his last eight at-bats, two away from the National League record shared by nine players.
Kenny Lofton had three hits and two RBI for the Braves.
In Los Angeles, John Olerud went 4-for-4 with two runs scored and an RBI while Bobby Jones pitched eight solid innings for his second win as the New York Mets defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers, 5-3.
Todd Hundley and Bernard Gilkey drove in two runs apiece for the Mets. Greg McMichael worked a 1-2-3 ninth for his first save.
"Just location," Dodgers manager Bill Russell responded when asked what was wrong with Valdes' performance. "Olerud came up in the right spot and Johnson was getting on base in front of him."
"I felt good," said Olerud. "He (Valdes) came after me with a lot of fastballs. "He tried to get ahead early. I'm trying to get more out of my lower body and I had a real good spring."

In San Diego, Steve Cooke, Rich Loiselle and John Ericks combined on a one-hitter and Tony Womack's two-run triple accounted for all the scoring as the Pittsburgh Pirates blanked the San Diego Padres, 2-0.

Cooke (1-1) allowed one hit, walked one and struck out three in seven innings for his first win since July 10th, 1994 as he improved to 2-2 lifetime against the Padres. Cooke threw just 73 pitches and retired 12 consecutive batters before he was replaced by Loiselle to begin the eighth.
"I worked my butt off to get back to this point," said Cooke missed all of 1995 with shoulder trouble and pitched just three games last season.
In St Louis, Willie McGee's solo homer with two outs in the bottom of the ninth inning lifted the St. Louis Cardinals to their first win of the season, 2-1 over the Montreal Expos.

Ugueth Urbina (1-1) got Tom Lampkin to foul out and struck out Roberto Mejia on three pitches to begin the ninth before McGee hit his first pitch over the right-field wall for his first home run of the season.

"You dream of things like that, but I'm not that type of hitter," McGee said. "I've always been strong enough but I'm a line-drive hitter that's why I think I've been consistent over the years because I stay within myself."
Reliever Mark Petkovsek (1-1) limited Montreal to two hits and struck out three over four scoreless innings for the victory.
In San Francisco, Scott Rolen's two-out single in the seventh scored Gregg Jefferies with the go-ahead run as the Philadelphia Phillies nipped the San Francisco Giants, 2-1.
Mark Leiter (1-1) became the first person other than Curt Schilling to win for Philadelphia, giving up an unearned run and three hits over seven innings for his first win against his former team.
Ricky Bottalico struck out three of the four batters he faced for his third save.
